result:
Solutions 1 and 3 are the more defensible pair, and Solution 1 is the cleaner of the two. All three agree on p = 2, ρ = 22, d = −4, so they differ only in P_X(t).

**Shared part (p, ρ, d).** A K3 surface in characteristic 0 has no nonzero symmetric differentials, so p > 0. The known positive-characteristic examples with these properties are supersingular in characteristic 2 with Artin invariant σ = 1. This gives ρ = 22 and, by Artin's formula, d = −p^{2σ} = −4. I accept this as the intended answer.

**Solution 2 (P = 1/(1−t⁴)).** This relies on the claim that K3 surfaces have no nonzero global vector fields in any characteristic. That is false: Rudakov–Shafarevich and later work show that supersingular K3 surfaces in characteristic 2 can carry global vector fields. The degree-4 generator is also asserted without justification, and the claim that Sym² has no sections is not established. I therefore reject this solution.

**Solutions 1 and 3 (P = 1/(1−t)).** Suppose 0 ≠ α ∈ H⁰(Ω¹). Its zero scheme Z is 0-dimensional, and c₂ = 24 gives length 24. The quotient Q = Ω/Oα is torsion-free of rank 1 with trivial determinant, so Q ≅ I_Z. The filtration F^j = α^j·Sym^{m−j}Ω of Sym^m Ω has graded pieces that are quotients of Sym^{m−j}(I_Z). Each has no global sections for m − j ≥ 1, because a nonzero global section would be a constant vanishing on Z. The bottom piece is O·α^m ≅ O, which contributes exactly one dimension. So dim H⁰(Sym^m Ω) ≤ 1, with equality since α^m ≠ 0. This gives P = 1/(1−t).

The gap in this argument is the hypothesis: it needs H⁰(Ω¹) ≠ 0. The problem only assumes some H⁰(Sym^m Ω) ≠ 0. Solutions 1 and 3 do not justify that a nonzero section of Ω¹ must exist, but they produce a self-consistent answer that matches the structure of the known examples. Solution 1 presents this more cleanly, and Solution 3 adds unsupported remarks about quasi-elliptic surfaces. I therefore prefer Solution 1, with moderate confidence.

CHOICE: 1
